name: MD-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+10 district with a sitting Democratic incumbent
Lopsided fundraising: Olszewski about $1.0M raised vs Wallace about $20K
Polymarket prices the Democratic side near 94%
No public polling and no outside spending against the incumbent
model.rationale: The district's D+10 lean, a first-term Democratic incumbent, and a roughly fifty-to-one fundraising gap leave Republican Dave Wallace without a visible path; markets and fundamentals both point to a victory in the neighborhood of twenty points.
model.watch: A major outside-spending push against Olszewski or an unusually strong Republican national environment could narrow the margin, though it would need to be historically large to put the seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 2nd District leans Democratic by ten points, and incumbent Johnny Olszewski is seeking re-election with the advantages of holding the seat. He has raised about $1.0 million and reports more than $600,000 on hand, while Republican Dave Wallace has raised roughly $20,000 and has only a few thousand dollars left. No outside groups have spent against the incumbent.

With no general-election polls available, the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the funding gap. Betting markets put the Democratic side's chances at roughly 94 percent. Those fundamentals point to a comfortable Olszewski win, with the open question being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
